main.title: Mortal Kombat X
main.subtitle: Three variations for every fighter
main.summary: Mortal Kombat X gives each fighter three variations, expanding tactical choices alongside a story that introduces a new generation.

cards.heading: A fighter with three variations
cards.text: Mortal Kombat X is NetherRealm?s 2015 fighting game, released on April 14 for PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Windows. Each fighter has three variations that change their available tools. The campaign brings younger characters into the continuing conflict alongside the series? veterans.

cards.heading: Choosing a different set of tools
cards.text: Choosing a variation can add weapons, summons, stances or other ways to control space. Two players using the same fighter can therefore approach a round with different tools. Opponents need to recognise both the character and the selected variation.

cards.heading: The next generation joins the conflict
cards.text: Cassie Cage, Jacqui Briggs, Takeda and Kung Jin join the older fighters. Their family ties and training connect them to existing characters while giving the campaign new relationships and rivalries. The roster carries the story forward through a younger generation.

cards.heading: X-Ray attacks and violent spectacle
cards.text: X-Ray attacks show the impact on bones and organs in close-up. Spending the required meter triggers a sequence of heavy blows before the fight returns to its usual view. These attacks sit alongside the series? elaborate finishing Fatalities.

main.title: Bravely Second: End Layer
main.subtitle: Silicon Studio · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Bravely Second: End Layer is Silicon Studio's Nintendo 3DS role-playing sequel to Bravely Default. Yew Geneolgia sets out to rescue Agnès Oblige after her abduction by the Kaiser. Returning heroes Tiz and Edea join him alongside Magnolia, a visitor from the moon. The party travels through Luxendarc, meeting people whose professions can become abilities for the group. The adventure retains the first game's deliberate turn-based battles, where preparing several actions in advance can be as important as choosing the strongest attack available now.

cards.heading: Another journey through Luxendarc
cards.text: Bravely Second: End Layer is Silicon Studio's Nintendo 3DS role-playing sequel to Bravely Default. Yew Geneolgia sets out to rescue Agnès Oblige after her abduction by the Kaiser. Returning heroes Tiz and Edea join him alongside Magnolia, a visitor from the moon. The party travels through Luxendarc, meeting people whose professions can become abilities for the group. The adventure retains the first game's deliberate turn-based battles, where preparing several actions in advance can be as important as choosing the strongest attack available now.

cards.heading: Borrow a turn or keep one for later
cards.text: Default makes a character defend and save a Brave Point. Brave spends those points to take several actions together, including borrowing against future turns. A decisive combination can end a fight quickly, but a surviving opponent may then face a party unable to respond. Jobs supply the abilities that make those combinations useful. Changing professions and mixing learned skills lets the player build different roles, turning the party into a plan whose parts need to cover one another when a gamble fails.

cards.heading: Keep fighting while the advantage lasts
cards.text: After winning an encounter in a single turn, the player can continue directly into another battle for greater rewards. The invitation makes efficiency useful, while the next fight tests whether the party has enough resources left to repeat its success. Job side stories also place competing characters around an ethical disagreement, with a choice determining which profession becomes available first. Ryo's music accompanies the journey. The sequel expands its predecessor through these decisions about continuation: when to spend, when to stop and which opportunity to pursue before another opens.

main.title: Xenoblade Chronicles X
main.subtitle: Human survivors on an unfamiliar planet
main.summary: Xenoblade Chronicles X is Monolith Soft's open-world role-playing game, first released for Wii U in Japan on 29 April 2015.

cards.heading: Human survivors on an unfamiliar planet
cards.text: Xenoblade Chronicles X is Monolith Soft's open-world role-playing game, first released for Wii U in Japan on 29 April 2015. Survivors of Earth's destruction establish New Los Angeles on the planet Mira, and the player's created character joins BLADE to explore and protect their new home. Five continents surround the settlement with enormous creatures, striking terrain and signs of other civilizations. The journey makes discovery a practical task for the surviving community, connecting the next expedition to humanity's effort to understand where it has landed.

cards.heading: Survey the world before crossing it
cards.text: Exploration, quests and resource gathering build the relationship between the city and the wider planet. The party moves through Mira's changing environments while real-time battles combine ordinary attacks with selected Arts and other systems. Learning a creature's strength or finding a route through an unfamiliar region matters to deciding which objective can be attempted next. The open landscape lets distant sights become long-term destinations, with the player's growing capabilities gradually turning the outline of the world into places that can actually be reached.

cards.heading: A machine changes the scale of exploration
cards.text: Skells add pilotable machines that change both travel and combat, eventually opening flight across terrain first encountered from the ground. Hiroyuki Sawano composed the soundtrack. Production began after Xenoblade Chronicles, with Tetsuya Takahashi and returning staff pursuing a much larger explorable world. The original Wii U version reached Western audiences that December; an expanded Definitive Edition followed on Switch in 2025. Its defining progression is spatial as well as statistical: the same planet acquires another scale when a route once crossed on foot can be seen and traveled from above.

main.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
main.subtitle: Geralt searches for Ciri in an open world shaped by choices and folklore
main.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt‍ is a 2015 action role-playing game developed and published by CD Projekt.

cards.heading: Geralt returns to an open world
cards.text: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is CD Projekt's 2015 action role-playing game, following monster hunter Geralt of Rivia as he searches for his adopted daughter Ciri. It continues the earlier Witcher games in an open world based on Andrzej Sapkowski's novels. Quests, conversations and combat lead Geralt through a setting shaped by Slavic folklore, with choices along the way affecting the story's outcome.

cards.heading: Choices, folklore and a search for Ciri
cards.text: The game takes place in a fictional fantasy world based on Slavic folklore. Players control Geralt of Rivia, a monster slayer for hire known as a Witcher, and search for his adopted daughter, Ciri, who is on the run from the Wild Hunt. Players battle the game's many dangers with weapons and magic, interact with non-player characters, and complete quests to acquire experience points and gold, which are used to increase Geralt's abilities and purchase equipment. The game's story has three possible endings, determined by the player's choices at key points in the narrative. Development began in 2011 and lasted for three and a half years. Central and Northern European cultures formed the basis of the game's world. The game was developed using the REDengine 3. The music was primarily composed by Marcin Przybyłowicz and performed by the Brandenburg State Orchestra.

cards.heading: Expansions and later editions
cards.text: The game launched on PlayStation 4, Windows and Xbox One in May 2015. Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine extended the adventure, and the 2016 Game of the Year Edition gathered them with the base game. Switch followed in 2019, with PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series editions arriving in 2022. Reviewers praised the quests, world and characters while also noting technical problems. Its reception made the relationship between local stories and the larger journey a central part of its reputation.

main.title: Splatoon
main.subtitle: Ink changes the ground and the way battles are fought
main.summary: Ink is both a weapon and a route through the map. Nintendo’s 2015 Wii U shooter links territory control, movement and transformation in four-player teams of Inklings.

cards.heading: Inklings and ink on Wii U
cards.text: Splatoon is Nintendo?s 2015 third-person shooter for Wii U. Four-player teams of Inklings use ink-firing weapons to cover the ground and fight opponents. In humanoid form they shoot; in squid form they swim through their own ink and hide beneath its surface. A separate single-player campaign accompanies the online modes.

cards.heading: From the first game to a series
cards.text: The first game in the series, Splatoon, was released for the Wii U on 28 May 2015. A sequel, Splatoon 2, was released for the Nintendo Switch on 21 July 2017, followed by an expansion pack, Octo Expansion, on 13 June 2018. A third game, Splatoon 3, was released on 9 September 2022, followed by an expansion pack titled Side Order, on 22 February 2024. A spin-off game, Splatoon Raiders, was released on 23 July 2026 as an exclusive for the Nintendo Switch 2. The series has received positive reviews for its style, gameplay mechanics and soundtrack, the first two games in the series having been nominated and awarded several year-end accolades from various gaming publications. The series has sold over 30 million copies.

cards.heading: Manga, concerts and competition
cards.text: Splatoon has spawned numerous collaborations with third-party companies and established its own esports tournament circuit in 2018. It has spawned a manga series as well as holographic music concerts, primarily in Japan.

main.title: Tabletop Simulator
main.subtitle: A shared table where pieces and rules stay in the players’ hands
main.summary: Tabletop Simulator is an independent video game that allows players to play and create tabletop games in a multiplayer physics sandbox.

cards.heading: Tabletop games inside a physics sandbox
cards.text: Tabletop Simulator is an independent video game that allows players to play and create tabletop games in a multiplayer physics sandbox. Developed by Berserk Games as their first title after a successful crowdfunding campaign in February 2014, the game was released in June of the following year.

cards.heading: Pieces with physical weight
cards.text: Tabletop Simulator is a player-driven physics sandbox, without set victory or failure conditions. After selecting a table to play on, players interact with the game by spawning and moving virtual pieces, which are subject to a physics simulation. Online multiplayer is supported with a maximum of ten players. Aside from spawning and moving pieces, the game includes mechanics to assist with common styles of board game play, such as automatic dice rolling and hiding players' pieces from one another; other mechanics aid in administrating a game, for example saving the state of the board or undoing moves.

cards.heading: A shared tabletop
cards.text: Several games are included, including chess, checkers and poker. Tables and pieces can be mixed and customized to create new games, which can then be saved to share and play with others. The game allows images and models to be imported to create entirely new pieces and tables, allowing for the recreation of most real-world board games. Over three-thousand games and custom assets are shared on the game's Steam Workshop; while there is original content, a notable number of these shared items are adaptations of existing games, including unlicensed derivatives of copyrighted works. Berserk Games has also worked with a number of game publishers to offer officially-licensed Tabletop Simulator versions of their games as downloadable content, such as Cosmic Encounter.

cards.heading: Building a physics sandbox
cards.text: Tabletop Simulator was developed by Berserk Games, a studio consisting of Jason Henry and Kimiko. Before forming Berserk Games, Henry attended college focusing on engineering, while working on game mods in his spare time, including the popular Mana Warfare mod for Chivalry: Medieval Warfare. Kimiko had been a community moderator for Chivalry and later a member of Torn Banner Studios. In an interview with Gamasutra, the pair described the game Desperate Gods as being an inspiration, though they wanted to expand the "free-form shared board game" concept to cover all tabletop games.
